Reading is still immediate.", "hint": "always @(posedge clk) if (we) mem[addr] <= din; assign dout = mem[addr];", "files": [{"name": "design.v", "src": "module ram16(input clk, input we, input [3:0] addr, input [7:0] din, output [7:0] dout);\n  // TODO\n  assign dout = 8'd0;\nendmodule\n", "edit": true}, {"name": "tb.v", "src": "`timescale 1ns/1ps\nmodule tb;\n  reg clk = 0;\n  reg we = 0;\n  reg [3:0] addr = 0;\n  reg [7:0] din = 0;\n  wire [7:0] dout;\n  ram16 dut(.clk(clk), .we(we), .addr(addr), .din(din), .dout(dout));\n  integer errs = 0;\n  task tick; begin #2 clk = 1; #3 clk = 0; #2; end endtask\n  initial begin\n    $dumpfile(\"dump.vcd\"); $dumpvars(0, tb);\n    #1;\n    we = 1'd1; addr = 4'd3; din = 8'd77; #1;\n    tick;\n    addr = 4'd9; din = 8'd200; #1;\n    tick;\n    we = 1'd0; addr = 4'd3; #1;\n    if (dout !== 8'd77) begin errs = errs + 1; $display(\"FAIL [read 3]: dout=%0d, expected 77\", dout); end\n    addr = 4'd9; #1;\n    if (dout !== 8'd200) begin errs = errs + 1; $display(\"FAIL [read 9]: dout=%0d, expected 200\", dout); end\n    addr = 4'd3; din = 8'd5; #1;\n    tick;\n    if (dout !== 8'd77) begin errs = errs + 1; $display(\"FAIL [no write when we=0]: dout=%0d, expected 77\", dout); end\n    if (errs == 0) $display(\"ALL PASS\"); else $display(\"%0d checks failed\", errs);\n    #5 $finish;\n  end\nendmodule\n", "edit": false}], "solution": {"design.v": "module ram16(input clk, input we, input [3:0] addr, input [7:0] din, output [7:0] dout);\n  reg [7:0] mem [0:15];\n  always @(posedge clk) begin\n    if (we) mem[addr] <= din;\n  end\n  assign dout = mem[addr];\nendmodule\n"}, "goals": [{"t": "It compiles", "re": "COMPILE"}, {"t": "Every test row passes (ALL PASS)", "re": "ALL PASS"}], "gen": "2005"}]};</script><script>/* Verilog lab UI: levels with editable files, Run, console, waveform and goals. Config in window.VLCFG. */
(function () {
  const CFG = window.VLCFG, L = CFG.levels, key = 'vlab:' + CFG.title;
  let done = {}, saved = {}, cur = 0, tab = 0, files = [], last = null, completed = false, busy = false;
  try { const s = JSON.parse(localStorage.getItem(key) || '{}'); done = s.done || {}; saved = s.code || {}; } catch (e) { }
  const $ = s => document.querySelector(s);
  const esc = s => s.replace(/[&<>]/g, c => ({ '&': '&', '<': '<', '>': '>' }[c]));
  document.body.innerHTML = '<div class="card"><h2>' + esc(CFG.title) + '</h2><div class="k" id="intro"></div></div><div class="card"><div class="chips" id="chips"></div><div id="lt"></div></div>' +
    '<div class="card"><div class="tabs" id="tabs"></div><textarea id="ed" spellcheck="false" autocapitalize="off" autocomplete="off" autocorrect="off"></textarea>' +
    '<div class="row"><button id="run">Run</button><button class="s" id="hint">Hint</button><button class="s" id="sol">Show solution</button><button class="s" id="rst">Start over</button></div>' +
    '<div id="hintbox" class="small"></div></div>' +
    '<div class="card"><b>Goals</b><ul id="goals"></ul><div id="status" class="small"></div></div>' +
    '<div class="card"><b>Console</b><pre id="con">Press Run.</pre><b>Waveform</b><div class="small" id="wnote">Signals appear after a run that dumps a VCD.</div><div class="wave" id="wave"><canvas id="cv" height="10"></canvas></div><div class="row"><button class="s" id="zin">Zoom in</button><button class="s" id="zout">Zoom out</button></div></div>';
  $('#intro').textContent = CFG.intro || '';
  let zoom = 1;
  function save() { try { localStorage.setItem(key, JSON.stringify({ done: done, code: saved })); } catch (e) { } }
  function chips() {
    $('#chips').innerHTML = '';
    L.forEach(function (lv, i) { const b = document.createElement('button'); b.className = 'chip' + (i === cur ? ' on' : '') + (done[i] ? ' done' : ''); b.textContent = (done[i] ? '✓ ' : '') + (i + 1); b.onclick = function () { enter(i); }; $('#chips').appendChild(b); });
  }
  function tabs() {
    $('#tabs').innerHTML = '';
    files.forEach(function (f, i) { const b = document.createElement('button'); b.className = i === tab ? '' : 's'; b.textContent = f.name + (f.edit ? '' : ' (read only)'); b.onclick = function () { pull(); tab = i; push(); tabs(); }; $('#tabs').appendChild(b); });
  }
  function pull() { if (files[tab]) files[tab].src = $('#ed').value; }
  function push() { const f = files[tab]; $('#ed').value = f.src; $('#ed').readOnly = !f.edit; }
  function goalsView(res) {
    $('#goals').innerHTML = '';
    L[cur].goals.forEach(function (g, i) { const li = document.createElement('li'); const ok = res && res[i]; li.className = ok ? 'ok' : ''; li.textContent = (ok ? '✓ ' : '○ ') + g.t; $('#goals').appendChild(li); });
  }
  function enter(i) {
    cur = i; const lv = L[i];
    files = lv.files.map(function (f) { const s = saved[i + ':' + f.name]; return { name: f.name, src: (f.edit && s != null) ? s : f.src, edit: !!f.edit }; });
    tab = Math.max(0, files.findIndex(function (f) { return f.edit; }));
    $('#lt').innerHTML = '<b>' + esc(lv.title) + '</b><div class="info" style="margin-top:4px">' + lv.text.split('\n').map(function (p) { return '<p style="margin:4px 0">' + esc(p) + '</p>'; }).join('') + '</div>';
    $('#hintbox').textContent = ''; $('#con').textContent = 'Press Run.'; $('#status').textContent = ''; last = null;
    tabs(); push(); goalsView(null); chips(); drawWave(null);
  }
  function evalGoals(r) {
    return L[cur].goals.map(function (g) {
      if (g.re === 'COMPILE') return r.ok;
      return r.ok && new RegExp(g.re, 'm').test(r.log);
    });
  }
  async function run() {
    if (busy) return last; busy = true; pull();
    files.forEach(function (f) { if (f.edit) saved[cur + ':' + f.name] = f.src; });
    $('#run').disabled = true; $('#status').textContent = 'compiling and simulating…';
    let r;
    try { r = await VL.run(files.map(function (f) { return { name: f.name, src: f.src }; }), L[cur].gen); } catch (e) { r = { ok: false, log: 'engine error: ' + e, vcd: null }; }
    last = r; $('#con').innerHTML = (r.ok ? '' : '<span class="err">') + esc(r.log.replace(/^VCD info:.*\n?/m, '').replace(/^\/[\w.]+:\d+: \$finish called at.*$/m, '').trim() || '(no output)') + (r.ok ? '' : '</span>');
    const res = evalGoals(r); goalsView(res);
    const all = res.every(Boolean);
    $('#status').textContent = r.ok ? (all ? 'Level complete.' : 'Compiled. Not all goals met yet.') : 'Compile error: fix it and run again.';
    if (all) { done[cur] = 1; }
    save(); chips(); drawWave(r.vcd);
    if (!completed && L.every(function (x, i) { return done[i]; })) { completed = true; try { if (window.lilith && window.lilith.complete) window.lilith.complete(); } catch (e) { } }
    $('#run').disabled = false; busy = false; return r;
  }
  function solve(i) {
    if (i !== cur) enter(i);
    const lv = L[cur];
    files.forEach(function (f) { if (lv.solution[f.name] != null) f.src = lv.solution[f.name]; });
    push(); return run();
  }
  /* ---- waveform ---- */
  function parseVCD(t) {
    const vars = {}, order = [], scope = []; let time = 0, end = 0; const lines = t.split('\n'); let defs = true;
    for (let ln of lines) {
      ln = ln.trim(); if (!ln) continue;
      if (defs) {
        if (ln.startsWith('$scope')) scope.push(ln.split(/\s+/)[2]);
        else if (ln.startsWith('$upscope')) scope.pop();
        else if (ln.startsWith('$var')) { const p = ln.split(/\s+/); const id = p[3]; if (!vars[id]) { vars[id] = { name: p[4], w: +p[2], depth: scope.length, ev: [] }; order.push(id); } }
        else if (ln.startsWith('$enddefinitions')) defs = false;
        continue;
      }
      const c = ln[0];
      if (c === '#') { time = +ln.slice(1); if (time > end) end = time; }
      else if (c === 'b' || c === 'B') { const p = ln.split(/\s+/); if (vars[p[1]]) vars[p[1]].ev.push([time, p[0].slice(1)]); }
      else if ('01xXzZ'.indexOf(c) >= 0) { const id = ln.slice(1); if (vars[id]) vars[id].ev.push([time, c]); }
    }
    return { vars: vars, order: order, end: end };
  }
  function valAt(v, t) { let r = 'x'; for (let k = 0; k < v.ev.length; k++) { if (v.ev[k][0] <= t) r = v.ev[k][1]; else break; } return r; }
  function hex(b) { if (/[xz]/i.test(b)) return b.toLowerCase().indexOf('x') >= 0 ? 'x' : 'z'; return parseInt(b, 2).toString(16); }
  function drawWave(vcd) {
    const cv = $('#cv'); const ctx = cv.getContext('2d');
    if (!vcd) { cv.width = 10; cv.height = 10; $('#wnote').style.display = ''; return; }
    const W = parseVCD(vcd); const ids = W.order.filter(function (id) { return W.vars[id].ev.length; }).slice(0, 16);
    if (!ids.length) { cv.width = 10; cv.height = 10; return; }
    $('#wnote').style.display = 'none';
    const rowH = 30, lab = 76, base = Math.max(300, $('#wave').clientWidth || 300), width = Math.floor((base - lab) * zoom) + lab, H = ids.length * rowH + 22;
    cv.width = width; cv.height = H; ctx.fillStyle = '#0a0712'; ctx.fillRect(0, 0, width, H);
    const end = W.end || 1, X = t => lab + (t / end) * (width - lab - 6);
    ctx.font = '11px ui-monospace,monospace'; ctx.textBaseline = 'middle';
    ctx.strokeStyle = '#2a2040'; ctx.fillStyle = '#7d72a0';
    const step = Math.pow(10, Math.floor(Math.log10(end / 5 || 1))) * (end / 5 / Math.pow(10, Math.floor(Math.log10(end / 5 || 1))) > 5 ? 5 : end / 5 / Math.pow(10, Math.floor(Math.log10(end / 5 || 1))) > 2 ? 2 : 1);
    for (let t = 0; t <= end; t += step) { ctx.beginPath(); ctx.moveTo(X(t), 14); ctx.lineTo(X(t), H); ctx.stroke(); ctx.fillText(String(t), X(t) + 2, 7); }
    ids.forEach(function (id, r) {
      const v = W.vars[id], y0 = 22 + r * rowH, yh = y0 + 6, yl = y0 + rowH - 8;
      ctx.fillStyle = '#d6ccf0'; ctx.fillText(v.name.slice(0, 10), 4, y0 + rowH / 2);
      const evs = v.ev.slice(); const pts = evs.map(function (e) { return e[0]; });
      for (let k = 0; k < evs.length; k++) {
        const x1 = X(evs[k][0]), x2 = X(k + 1 < evs.length ? evs[k + 1][0] : end), val = evs[k][1];
        const bad = /[xz]/i.test(val);
        ctx.strokeStyle = bad ? '#ff7a9a' : '#7be0a4'; ctx.lineWidth = 1.5;
        if (v.w === 1) {
          const y = (val === '1') ? yh : (val === '0' ? yl : (yh + yl) / 2);
          ctx.beginPath(); ctx.moveTo(x1, y); ctx.lineTo(x2, y); ctx.stroke();
          if (k > 0) { const pv = evs[k - 1][1], py = (pv === '1') ? yh : (pv === '0' ? yl : (yh + yl) / 2); ctx.beginPath(); ctx.moveTo(x1, py); ctx.lineTo(x1, y); ctx.stroke(); }
        } else {
          ctx.beginPath(); ctx.moveTo(x1 + 2, (yh + yl) / 2); ctx.lineTo(x1 + 5, yh); ctx.lineTo(x2 - 3, yh); ctx.lineTo(x2, (yh + yl) / 2); ctx.lineTo(x2 - 3, yl); ctx.lineTo(x1 + 5, yl); ctx.closePath(); ctx.stroke();
          if (x2 - x1 > 16) { ctx.fillStyle = bad ? '#ff7a9a' : '#ffd27f'; ctx.fillText(hex(val), x1 + 8, (yh + yl) / 2); }
        }
      }
    });
  }
  $('#run').onclick = function () { run(); };
  $('#hint').onclick = function () { $('#hintbox').textContent = 'Hint: ' + L[cur].hint; };
  $('#sol').onclick = function () { const lv = L[cur]; files.forEach(function (f) { if (lv.solution[f.name] != null) f.src = lv.solution[f.name]; }); push(); $('#hintbox').textContent = 'Solution loaded. Press Run to check it, and read it line by line.'; };
  $('#rst').onclick = function () { saved = {}; Object.keys(saved).forEach(function (k) { delete saved[k]; }); enter(cur); };
  $('#zin').onclick = function () { zoom = Math.min(16, zoom * 2); if (last) drawWave(last.vcd); };
  $('#zout').onclick = function () { zoom = Math.max(1, zoom / 2); if (last) drawWave(last.vcd); };
  $('#ed').addEventListener('keydown', function (e) { if (e.key === 'Tab') { e.preventDefault(); const t = e.target, s = t.selectionStart; t.value = t.value.slice(0, s) + '  ' + t.value.slice(t.selectionEnd); t.selectionStart = t.selectionEnd = s + 2; } });
  window.__lab = { lab: CFG, enter: enter, run: run, solve: solve, isDone: function (i) { return !!done[i]; }, setCode: function (n, s) { files.forEach(function (f) { if (f.name === n) { f.src = s; } }); push(); } };
  $('#rst').onclick = function () { Object.keys(saved).forEach(function (k) { if (k.indexOf(cur + ':') === 0) delete saved[k]; }); enter(cur); };
  enter(0);
})();
</script></body></html>

chapters.title: From RTL to silicon, and a tiny CPU to prove it
summary: You can now describe hardware. This last chapter shows where it goes: which Verilog the tools can turn into gates, how an FPGA or an ASIC is made from it, and how timing is checked.

Then we use everything you have learnt to build a complete 8-bit processor, one block at a time: ALU, program counter, control decoder and top level. You finish by writing a program for the CPU you made.
This is the point of the whole course: an idea described in a few dozen lines, simulated, and ready to become silicon.

glossary.def: Turning RTL into a netlist of gates and flip-flops from a library.
The part of Verilog that tools can turn into hardware.
Checking that every path meets its clock period without simulating.
The configuration data loaded into an FPGA.
The layout file sent to a chip factory.
Instruction set architecture: the instructions a processor understands.
The parts that hold and transform data, and the part that tells them what to do.

keyPoints: Synthesis turns RTL into a gate netlist; FPGA and ASIC flows then place and route it.
Write synthesisable RTL: clocked always blocks with <=, combinational with =, no delays, fixed loops.
Static timing analysis checks every path against the clock period.
A CPU is a datapath (registers, ALU) plus control that decodes instructions.
Fetch, decode, execute, write back: one instruction per clock in our tiny CPU.

items: Quick recap of the last chapter, Building big: hierarchy, parameters, generate, functions and memories:
• module m #(parameter N = 8)(...) makes the width a knob; instantiate with m #(.N(12)).
• generate for (genvar) repeats hardware at compile time.
• A function returns a value computed from its inputs, with no delays.
• A memory is an array: reg [7:0] mem [0:15]; read it with mem[addr].
• Write once, reuse many times: that is the aim of every feature here.

ELI5. Imagine you have drawn a house on paper and you want to build it for real. You need a builder to turn the drawing into bricks, an inspector to check it will stand, and a place to build. That is what happens to a chip design.

Now the real words. Synthesis turns RTL into gates and flip-flops. Then either an FPGA tool places them into programmable blocks and makes a bitstream, or an ASIC flow builds a full layout for a factory.

Timing tools check every path against the clock. To prove you can do it all, you build a tiny 8-bit processor: a program counter, a memory with the program, a control block that decodes instructions, and an ALU that calculates.
Try it. In the lab write your own program in the ROM so the CPU prints 4, 3, 2, 1.
If you remember one thing: you can build a real processor from the same simple parts: registers, logic and a state machine.

Your simulation passes. What now? The design goes through synthesis. A synthesis tool reads your Verilog, works out what hardware you meant, and maps it onto the gates and flip-flops of a target library.
The result is a netlist: a long list of gates and the wires between them. You also give it constraints, such as the clock speed you want and the pins to use. (See Figure 14.1 below.)

lesson.caption: Figure 14.1. After synthesis the flow splits. An FPGA flow places the netlist into programmable logic and produces a bitstream. An ASIC flow produces a full layout.

items: For an FPGA, the next steps are place and route: assign each gate to a lookup table somewhere on the chip and connect them through the programmable wiring. The tool outputs a bitstream, which you load into the chip.
For an ASIC, the steps are longer: floorplanning, placement, clock tree building, routing, and a long list of checks, ending in the layout file sent to the factory. (See Table 14.1 below.)

lesson.title: Table 14.1. FPGA flow versus ASIC flow
head: Step
FPGA
ASIC
rows: timing, power, design rules, layout versus schematic
GDSII file, then weeks in a factory

items: Not all Verilog can be synthesised. Delays like #5 are ignored. Initial blocks mostly are not hardware, apart from setting FPGA starting values. Loops need a fixed count. Dividing by a variable is huge.

The safe subset is: assign statements, combinational always @* blocks with blocking assignment, clocked always blocks with non-blocking assignment, parameters, generate loops and instances. This course used this subset in every design lab. (See Table 14.2 below.)

lesson.title: Table 14.2. What synthesis understands
head: Construct
Becomes
Careful
rows: assign every output on every path

items: How does the tool know your design is fast enough? Static timing analysis. It does not simulate. It adds up the delays along every path from one flip-flop to the next using the library numbers, and compares each sum to the clock period. A path with negative slack fails.
The report lists the worst paths, which are your critical paths, and tells you where to improve the design.
Now the best part. Let us build something real: an 8-bit accumulator CPU. It has one 8-bit register, the accumulator, and a small ROM holding the program.

Each instruction is eight bits: the upper four bits are the opcode and the lower four bits are an operand. There are seven instructions: load immediate, add, subtract, and, jump if not zero, output, and halt. (See Figure 14.2 below.) (See Table 14.3 below.)

lesson.caption: Figure 14.2. The instruction format and the seven instructions of the tiny CPU.

lesson.title: Table 14.3. The tiny CPU's instructions
head: Hex
Name
Effect
rows: if acc is not 0, pc = a

items: The CPU is a datapath plus a controller. The datapath holds the data: the program counter pc, the instruction ROM, the accumulator and the ALU.

The controller is a decoder that looks at the opcode and sets the control signals: whether to load an immediate, which ALU operation to use, whether to jump, whether to output, whether to halt. (See Figure 14.3 below.)

lesson.caption: Figure 14.3. The tiny CPU. The program counter fetches from the ROM; the control decodes; the ALU computes; the accumulator stores.

items: Every clock cycle does one instruction. The pc supplies an address to the ROM, which gives back an instruction. The control block decodes it.

If it is an ALU instruction, the ALU combines the accumulator and the operand, and the result is written back to the accumulator at the clock edge. The pc then adds one, or jumps to the operand if a JNZ finds the accumulator not zero. HALT stops the pc.

The lab builds this CPU in five steps, each checked by its own testbench. First the ALU: a case statement. Second the program counter: a register with reset, enable and load. Third the control decoder: a case on the opcode.
Fourth the top level, wiring all of them together, running a program that adds 3, 4 and 5 to show 12. Fifth, you write your own program.

The last level is the best. You become the programmer. The ROM is the only thing you change, and you write the machine code by hand: 04, 50, 21, 41, 60. That is a loop that counts down from 4 and prints each value.
When your waveform shows 4, 3, 2, 1, you have designed hardware, tested it, and programmed it, with nothing but what this course taught you. (See Table 14.4 below.)

lesson.title: Table 14.4. Where to go next
head: Topic
What it adds
rows: a modern superset: logic type, always_ff, interfaces, assertions
run your designs on real hardware
Yosys, OpenROAD and open PDKs: from Verilog to GDSII for free
the other main language; the same ideas in a different syntax

items: A last word. The labs in this course run the Icarus Verilog compiler, compiled to WebAssembly by the VeriSim project, entirely inside your device. You can take any module from the course, paste it into a desktop copy of Icarus Verilog or an FPGA tool, and it will run.
Hardware design is a craft of habits: draw first, name things, simulate everything, keep it simple. Good luck.
Memory trick: Fetch, decode, execute, write. One CPU instruction: Fetch, Decode, Execute, Write back: 'FDEW'.

quiz.explain: The operand is in [3:0].

window.__VLM = {};
const VL = (function () {
  const B = window.VL_BLOBS;
  async function inflate(b64) {
    const bin = atob(b64), u = new Uint8Array(bin.length);
    for (let i = 0; i < bin.length; i++) u[i] = bin.charCodeAt(i);
    const ds = new DecompressionStream('deflate-raw');
    const w = ds.writable.getWriter(); w.write(u); w.close();
    return new Uint8Array(await new Response(ds.readable).arrayBuffer());
  }
  const wasm = {}; let ready = null;
  function load() {
    if (ready) return ready;
    ready = (async () => {
      for (const n of ['ivlpp', 'ivl', 'vvp']) {
        const js = new TextDecoder().decode(await inflate(B[n + '_js']));
        wasm[n] = await inflate(B[n + '_wasm']);
        const s = document.createElement('script'); s.textContent = js; document.head.appendChild(s);
      }
    })();
    return ready;
  }
  const mod = (n, o) => window.__VLM[n](Object.assign({ wasmBinary: wasm[n] }, o));
  const CONF = g => 'basedir:/\nmodule:system.vpi\ngeneration:' + g + '\ngeneration:no-specify\nout:/out.vvp\niwidth:32\nwidthcap:65536\nfunctor:cprop\nfunctor:nodangle\nflag:DLL=vvp.tgt\n';
  /* files: [{name, src}]; returns {ok, log, vcd, err} */
  async function run(files, gen) {
    await load(); gen = gen || '2005';
    const code = [];
    const pp = await mod('ivlpp', { print: s => code.push(s), printErr: () => {} });
    const args = ['-L'];
    for (const f of files) { pp.FS.writeFile('/' + f.name, f.src.endsWith('\n') ? f.src : f.src + '\n'); args.push('/' + f.name); }
    pp.callMain(args);
    const err = [];
    const c = await mod('ivl', { print: () => {}, printErr: s => err.push(s) });
    c.FS.writeFile('/ivl.conf', CONF(gen)); c.FS.writeFile('/src.v', code.join('\n') + '\n');
    try { c.callMain(['-C/ivl.conf', '--', '/src.v']); } catch (e) {}
    let vvp = null; try { vvp = c.FS.readFile('/out.vvp'); } catch (e) {}
    const eText = err.filter(l => !/system\.vpi|dynamic linking not enabled/.test(l)).join('\n');
    if (!vvp) return { ok: false, log: eText || 'compile failed', vcd: null, err: eText };
    const out = [];
    const v = await mod('vvp', { print: s => out.push(s), printErr: s => out.push(s) });
    v.FS.writeFile('/sim.vvp', vvp);
    try { v.callMain(['/sim.vvp']); } catch (e) {}
    let vcd = null; try { vcd = v.FS.readFile('/dump.vcd', { encoding: 'utf8' }); } catch (e) {}
    return { ok: true, log: out.join('\n'), vcd: vcd, err: eText };
  }
  return { run, load };
})();

practice.title: The tiny CPU
practice.intro: Match each block to its job.
pairs: holds the address of the next instruction

practice.title: To silicon
practice.text: A tool that turns RTL into gates is called {{synthesis}}. Checking every path against the clock period without simulating is {{static}} timing analysis. An FPGA is configured by loading a {{bitstream}}. A processor is a {{datapath}} plus a controller.

practice.title: One instruction
practice.intro: Order what the CPU does for each instruction.
items: pc addresses the ROM
the control decodes the opcode
the ALU or immediate produces a result
the accumulator updates and the pc moves on

sandbox.title: Verilog cheat sheet
sandbox.intro: A scripted lookup, not a simulator. Try: module, gates, numbers, operators, assign, always, ff, reset, case, fsm, clock, tb, delay, param, memory, flow, help

out: module     module name(input a, input b, output y);
gates      and (y,a,b); or (y,a,b); nand nor xor xnor
tb         no ports; reg inputs, wire outputs, DUT instance, initial be
memory     reg [7:0] mem [0:15];   16 words of 8 bits
flow       spec, architecture, RTL, simulate, synthesise, place and rou
module name(input a, input b, output y);
and (y,a,b); or (y,a,b); nand nor xor xnor
a continuous connection: y always follows the expression
left side must be a wire
assign every output on every path, or a latch appears
async: always @(posedge clk or negedge rst_n)
reset first in the if chain
Moore: from state; Mealy: state and input
no ports; reg inputs, wire outputs, DUT instance, initial begin ... end
dumpfile and dumpvars record a waveform; finish ends the run
genvar i; generate for (i=0;i<N;i=i+1) begin ... end endgenerate
write: always @(posedge clk) if (we) mem[addr] <= din;
